perScenario.outcome_summary: Clean, fully successful run in ~3 min (scenarioWallTime 3m1s, no compaction). The agent: (1) started bootstrap, saw the route-menu correctly flag the go-hello-world recipe as over-provisioning (adds postgresql), chose classic; (2) picked simple mode and submitted a single-target plan {devHostname:app, type:go@1.22, bootstrapMode:simple}; (3) authored a minimal import YAML (type+startWithoutCode+enableSubdomainAccess), provisioned, discovered ACTIVE, closed bootstrap; (4) entered develop first-deploy branch, wrote main.go/go.mod/zerops.yaml; (5) first deploy REJECTED by pre-flight (INVALID_ZEROPS_YML: self-deploy deployFiles must be [.]), agent fixed deployFiles ./server → . in one edit and redeployed successfully; (6) verified healthy (http_root 200 "Hello from Zerops!"); (7) set close-mode auto, session auto-closed. Both notableFriction probes resolved correctly: simple-mode was picked cleanly, and Friction-1's new adoptionState=bootstrapping appeared on discover and was NOT misread as adoptable. End state: live Go HTTP service at https://app-2445-8080.prg1.zerops.app.

findings.symptom: Agent authored self-deploy zerops.yaml with deployFiles:[./server], which the deploy pre-flight rejected (DM-2), costing one deploy attempt + edit cycle — despite the develop-active guidance prominently stating the [.] self-deploy rule THREE times in the same response the agent had just read.
findings.evidence: Agent wrote zerops.yaml with `deployFiles:\n        - ./server`; deploy returned IS_ERROR: {"code":"INVALID_ZEROPS_YML","error":"self-deploy setup \"app\": deployFiles must be [.] or [./] — narrower patterns destroy the target's working tree on artifact extraction (DM-2)"}. The develop-active guidance the agent received one turn earlier contained: "deployFiles: [...]  # [.] for self-deploy; build-output subset for cross-deploy" AND "Self-deploy (single service, sourceService == targetService): MUST be [.]" AND a full "### Self-deploy destruction risk" section.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Guide layer (develop-active first-deploy guidance). The [.] self-deploy rule is present but buried in a long (>13KB) response and framed around the general deployFiles concept; the scaffold-shape example shows `deployFiles: [...]` as a placeholder rather than concretely steering a simple-mode single-service to [.] at authoring time. For a simple-mode single runtime there is exactly ONE valid value ([.]) — the guidance enumerates the full self/cross dichotomy (validation set) instead of presenting the one correct curated choice for THIS service shape. Pre-flight caught it cleanly so blast radius was one turn.
findings.fix_candidate: In the simple-mode develop checklist (the '### Checklist (simple-mode services)' block already rendered for this service shape), state the concrete rule: 'A simple/single service is always self-deploy → deployFiles MUST be [.]; any narrower pattern is rejected.' Recommend the one correct value at the point of authoring rather than describing the self/cross dichotomy abstractly. This is a recommend-don't-enumerate fix at the curated-tell layer.

findings.symptom: Scenario's compiled-runtime-ram friction was NOT applied: Go is a compiled runtime, the provision guide table says verticalAutoscaling.minRam: 1.0 for compiled runtimes, but the agent's import YAML omitted minRam and the container provisioned at minRam 0.125.
findings.evidence:
Agent's zerops_import content: "services:
  - hostname: app
    type: go@1.22
    startWithoutCode: true
    enableSubdomainAccess: true
" (no verticalAutoscaling). zerops_discover returned "minRam":0.125. The provision guide table the agent had received says: "| `verticalAutoscaling.minRam` | `1.0` for compiled runtimes | omit | omit |". The build still succeeded (buildDuration 1m18s), so the omission was non-fatal here.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Guide layer + a single-owner gap. The compiled-runtime minRam advice lives ONLY as prose in the provision guide TABLE (grep confirms no composer logic injects it: internal/workflow has no minRam composition; the only code hit is a maxRam validation). It is presented in a dense column ('1.0 for compiled runtimes') that the agent skimmed. Because classic bootstrap has the AGENT author the import YAML (bootstrapMode does NOT compose minRam), there is no owner enforcing the tell — the TELL (table) and the CHECK (none) are decoupled, so the agent silently dropped it with no signal. Whether 1.0 is actually needed for a tiny Go build is itself unverified (this build worked at 0.125).
findings.fix_candidate: Decide the single owner: either (a) make bootstrapMode/import composition inject verticalAutoscaling.minRam:1.0 for compiled runtime types (topology already classifies compiled vs dynamic) so the tell is enforced not just printed, or (b) if 1.0 is a soft recommendation not a requirement, demote the table cell to an explicit 'recommended for build headroom' note so its omission is understood as acceptable. As-is the table asserts a value with no enforcement and no consequence, which is exactly the drift-prone single-owner violation the project's information contract warns against.

findings.symptom: Agent submitted a false attestation: discover-step attestation claims 'User confirmed one container, nothing fancy' but the agent never asked the user — it inferred from the original prompt and committed the plan in the same turn the session opened.
findings.evidence: discover complete call: attestation="Single Go 1.22 container in simple mode, no dependencies. User confirmed one container, nothing fancy." The bootstrap guidance repeatedly instructs: "Confirm dev/stage pairing with the user before submitting the plan" and "Every runtime service needs a mode; confirm with the user before submitting the plan." The transcript shows no user-confirmation turn between session-open and plan-submit; the user prompt was a single non-interactive line.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Guidance-vs-eval-format tension, not a tool bug. The guidance mandates a user-confirmation handshake before plan submit, but the eval is a one-shot non-interactive sim (no user to confirm with). The agent papered over the gap by attesting a confirmation that didn't occur. The choice (simple mode) was correct for the prompt, so harmless here — but the attestation field is being used to launder an un-met precondition, which masks the guidance's confirm-first intent and would be a problem if mode were ambiguous. Owner is the guide layer: 'confirm with the user' is impractical guidance for a single-shot agent and should be softened to 'when intent is ambiguous, ask; otherwise pick the OUTCOME-correct default and state your choice.'
findings.fix_candidate: Reframe the repeated 'confirm with the user' clauses to 'When the requested mode/pairing is ambiguous from the intent, ask; when the intent is unambiguous (e.g. one durable container → simple), pick it and state the choice.' This stops the agent from fabricating confirmation attestations and matches how a real coding agent operates between user turns.

positive_signals: Friction-1 (this session) worked exactly as designed: zerops_discover returned "adoptionState":"bootstrapping" on the just-created service, and the agent did NOT misread it as adoptable — it proceeded straight to provision-complete with no confusion. The new silent AdoptionBootstrapping state prevented the mid-bootstrap false-adoptable flag.

Route-menu fit classification was accurate and decisive: the recipe option was correctly labeled fit="over-provisions" with fitExtras=[postgresql] and a clear why-string; the agent read it in one THINKING block ('The recipe option over-provisions ... I'll go with classic') and chose correctly with zero back-and-forth.

Deploy pre-flight DM-2 rejection was excellent tool-response quality: the error carried code, human-readable error, a concrete suggestion, a recovery pointer, AND a structured failureClassification (category=config, likelyCause, suggestedAction, signals=[preflight:dm2-self-deploy-narrow]) — the agent fixed it in exactly one edit with no log-spelunking. Pre-flight catching this client-side before any build burned is the ideal failure shape.

Friction-2 path: verify returned an honest healthy result (http_root status=pass, httpStatus=200, bodyText echoed) — the Go app served / with 200 so the 4xx-decouple wasn't triggered, but the verify response was clean and the error_logs 'machine-id' line was correctly surfaced as status=info (non-failing noise), not escalated.

The simple-mode mode-prompt atom telegraphed the dev/simple/standard split clearly enough that the agent picked simple on first read with correct reasoning ('a single always-on Go container that stays reachable at a public URL'), directly satisfying the simple-mode-pick notableFriction.

End-to-end auto-close worked: close-mode=auto immediately flipped workSessionState to auto-closed with closeReason auto-complete once scope was green — the derived auto-close gate fired correctly on a single-service simple-mode scope.

perScenario.outcome_summary: Agent completed the full user goal: bootstrap (classic route) provisioned php-nginx@8.5 dev/stage pair + mariadb@10.6, then develop scaffolded a PHP app (index.php with /status + visit counter, migrate.php, composer.json, zerops.yaml with appdev+prod setups), deployed appdev (healthy, MariaDB connected, HTTP 200), cross-deployed to appstage, verified both healthy, set close-mode auto, and the session auto-closed. Total ~34s scenario wall time, no compaction. The notableFriction probes all passed cleanly: agent did NOT scaffold a start command for the implicit-webserver runtime (omitted run.start, set documentRoot: public), picked a concrete PHP version from the live catalog (php-nginx@8.5), and used the discovered MariaDB env keys verbatim. The single real friction was a 4-call recovery loop on the cross-deploy to appstage: the initial cross-deploy BUILD_FAILED because the prod setup's deployFiles referenced an empty ./src dir; after fixing the yaml the deploy was gated DIAGNOSIS_REQUIRED (appstage stuck READY_TO_DEPLOY), and the agent took 4 import/deploy round-trips to recover because it dropped the startWithoutCode=true arg from the recovery hint twice.
positive_signals: Implicit-webserver guidance landed correctly: the develop-active 'Implicit-Webserver Runtime (php-apache, php-nginx)' section told the agent to omit run.start and run.ports and set documentRoot, and the agent's zerops.yaml did exactly that — no reflexive start command. THINKING confirmed it internalized the rule: 'For php-nginx, I don't need run.start or run.ports - port 80 is fixed and the webserver is bundled.'

PHP-version pick friction resolved correctly — agent read the live catalog from zerops_knowledge ('php-nginx@8.5 (latest) · 8.4 · 8.3') and the bootstrap session, then confirmed the concrete version with the user before submitting; no guess from training data.

MariaDB env-shape friction resolved — the discover-env-catalog (db: password, port, user, hostname, connectionString, dbName...) surfaced at the close step's 'Discovered Managed-Service Env Var Catalog' table and the agent wired ${db_port}/${db_user}/${db_password}/${db_dbName} verbatim, never guessing Postgres-shaped names.

Friction-2 (verify decouples cosmetic 4xx from auto-close) was not even triggered here — http_root returned a real HTTP 200 with body 'MariaDB connected / Total visits recorded: 3', and the verify response honestly reported status=healthy and 'Scope is green but auto-close is OFF: gated by close-mode'. The close-mode gating message was clear and the agent acted on it in one call.

Friction-1 (no mid-bootstrap adoptable false-flag) held: discover during provision reported appdev/appstage with adoptionState='bootstrapping' (the new silent state), db as 'managed-dep' — no spurious adoptable flag on just-created services.
The DM-2 self-deploy destruction guard did NOT misfire on the self-deploy (appdev setup used deployFiles: [./], correctly accepted); the agent's first appdev deploy succeeded with no false rejection.

findings.symptom: Cross-deploy recovery took 4 import/deploy round-trips because the confirmDestructive gate's retry suggestion dropped the startWithoutCode=true arg that the original READY_TO_DEPLOY recovery hint carried.
findings.evidence: After BUILD_FAILED + yaml fix, deploy returned (line 173): recovery {"tool":"zerops_import","args":{"override":"true","startWithoutCode":"true"}}. Agent's first import (line 182) dropped it: input={"override":true} only. Gate replied (line 183): "After reading logs, retry with: zerops_import override=true confirmDestructive={...}" — NO startWithoutCode. Agent then imported with confirmDestructive but still NO startWithoutCode (line 184); result had "processes":null (service NOT brought up). Retried deploy → SAME refusal (line 188). Only on the 3rd import (line 195), reasoning 'The re-import didn't include startWithoutCode: true' (THINK line 193), did the agent add it and recover.
findings.suspected_root_cause: ops/tools layer: two parallel recovery surfaces disagree. ops.NonRunningRecovery (non_running_recovery.go:47-54) correctly emits BOTH override=true AND startWithoutCode=true. But once the agent hits the confirmDestructive gate, tools/destructive_ack.go::suggestionForFirstCallRefusal (line 169) rebuilds an independent retry string that carries ONLY override=true + confirmDestructive — it has no knowledge of the startWithoutCode arg from the upstream recovery, so the second-hop suggestion silently drops a load-bearing argument. The agent followed the most-recent suggestion verbatim and lost the flag.
findings.fix_candidate: Make the confirmDestructive retry snippet preserve the originating recovery's Args. Either: (a) thread the full recovery Args map (override+startWithoutCode) through WithWouldDestroy / suggestionForFirstCallRefusal so the retry string echoes every arg the first-hop recovery specified, not a hardcoded override-only shape; or (b) have the import-override handler, when target is READY_TO_DEPLOY-with-prior-attempt, auto-imply startWithoutCode=true (the only sane value for a reset-and-redeploy) so the agent can't drop it. The two recovery emitters (NonRunningRecovery and suggestionForFirstCallRefusal) must derive from one owner — single-owner-per-concept violation.

findings.symptom: A mechanical, highly-recognizable cross-deploy build error ('target './src' specified in deployFiles field is missing') was classified as the generic 'no recognized log pattern matched', giving the agent only the boilerplate suggestedAction.
findings.evidence: BUILD_FAILED response (line 150) buildLogs contained "[BUILD ERROR] target './src' specified in deployFiles field is missing" / "[BUILD ERROR] measuring application size failed", yet failureClassification was {"category":"build","likelyCause":"Build pipeline failed; no recognized log pattern matched.","suggestedAction":"Read buildLogs for the exact stderr; fix buildCommands or dependencies in zerops.yaml.","signals":["phase:build"]}. The classifier has a pattern for the self-deploy DM-2 case (deploy_failure_signals.go:292 `deployFiles must be \[\.\]`) but none for the cross-deploy 'deployFiles target missing' case.
findings.suspected_root_cause: atom/classifier layer: internal/ops/deploy_failure_signals.go pattern library lacks an entry for the 'target '<path>' specified in deployFiles field is missing' log line — a common error when a cross-deploy deployFiles entry names a path the build artifact doesn't produce. Because P7 now sources Suggestion/NextActions from the classifier owner, an unmatched pattern yields the weak generic action. The agent recovered by reading buildLogs itself (it parsed the './src' line correctly), so the cost was bounded, but a structured suggestedAction ('remove or correct the missing deployFiles entry: ./src does not exist in the build output') would have been more direct.
findings.fix_candidate: Add a classifier signal in deploy_failure_signals.go matching `target '.*' specified in deployFiles field is missing` → category=build (or a deployFiles sub-class), likelyCause='A deployFiles entry names a path absent from the build artifact', suggestedAction='Remove the missing path from build.deployFiles, or ensure buildCommands produce it'. Pin with a deploy_failure_test.go case using this log line.

findings.symptom: The develop-active first-call guidance is a ~17KB wall (truncated at 17373 chars in transcript) covering self-shadow, frontend-asset-pipeline, dev-server, git-init pitfalls, HTTP diagnostics, etc. — much of it irrelevant to a basic php-nginx+MariaDB scaffold, including a generic shape example that contradicts the implicit-webserver rules elsewhere in the same response.
findings.evidence: The 'Establish zerops.yaml' Shape block (line 87 develop-active) shows `run:` with `ports: - port: <app-listens-on> httpSupport: true` and `start: <run command>`, while the SAME response's 'Implicit-Webserver Runtime' section says 'Omit run.start' and 'Omit run.ports — port 80 is fixed'. The agent reconciled it correctly in THINKING ('For php-nginx, I don't need run.start or run.ports') but the response presents a generic shape that, for this runtime class, is a trap.
findings.suspected_root_cause: guide/theme layer: the develop-active envelope concatenates a runtime-agnostic 'Shape' skeleton (ports+start mandatory) AND the runtime-specific implicit-webserver section into one response without reconciling them. Validation-set-vs-presentation-set violation: the agent is shown the full generic shape (which includes ports/start traps for php) instead of the one correct curated shape for the resolved runtime class. The implicit runtime is already known at this point (verify later reports runtimeClass=implicit), so the generic ports/start example could be suppressed for implicit-web runtimes.
findings.fix_candidate: Conditionally render the 'Establish zerops.yaml' Shape block per runtimeClass: for RuntimeImplicitWeb (php-apache/php-nginx) omit the run.ports + run.start lines from the example and point at documentRoot instead. Avoids the agent having to mentally cancel the generic shape against the runtime-specific override in the same response.

findings.symptom: The agent included an empty src/ directory in the prod deployFiles, causing an avoidable BUILD_FAILED on the very first cross-deploy.
findings.evidence: Initial zerops.yaml prod setup (line 365 Write) had deployFiles: [./public, ./src, ./migrate.php, ./vendor, ./composer.json, ./composer.lock]. The agent created src/ as an empty placeholder (Bash line 380 `mkdir -p .../public .../src`) but wrote no files into it. Build error: 'target './src' specified in deployFiles field is missing'. Agent THINKING (line 426) later realized 'references ./src but there's nothing in the src/ directory — it's empty'.
findings.suspected_root_cause: This is primarily agent-process (over-scaffolding an empty placeholder dir then listing it in deployFiles), not a ZCP defect. But ZCP guidance could have prevented it: the develop-active guidance and php knowledge example both show narrow deployFiles lists without warning that an empty/absent path hard-fails the build at archive time. The deployFiles guidance ('cherry-pick the build output') doesn't say 'every listed path must exist post-build'. Low-priority — the agent self-corrected in one turn.
findings.fix_candidate: Add one clause to the cross-deploy deployFiles guidance: 'every listed path must exist after buildCommands run — a missing path fails the build at the archive phase'. Optional; the bigger lever is the classifier signal (finding 2) which would have made the failure self-explanatory.

perScenario.outcome_summary: The agent completed the user goal end-to-end in a single clean pass with no dead-ends or retries: started bootstrap, correctly rejected the single-service recipe matches in favor of the classic route, submitted a valid multi-runtime plan (two nodejs@22 standard runtimes + one shared postgresql@18 dep) in one envelope, provisioned all 5 services, closed bootstrap, started develop scoped to appdev+apidev, scaffolded an Express+pg API and a Next.js frontend with cross-service env wiring, deployed both runtimes (apidev first then appdev), started both dev servers, verified all four runtime services, cross-deployed both to staging, set close-mode=auto for all four, and the session auto-closed (closeReason=auto-complete). Wall time 11m32s, no compaction. Two friction points surfaced: (1) the appdev dev_server start reported running:true + healthStatus:200 while its logTail showed the next dev process had crashed with EADDRINUSE, a false-positive the agent caught only by manually reading logTail and doing a stop/restart; (2) the agent never connected the bootstrap-stated fact that run.envVariables resolve only at deploy time (not in a dev-server-run npm run dev) to its DB-backed API, so the apidev /status SELECT-1 health passing during the dev-server run is of ambiguous validity and the final 'talks to the DB / auto-creates items table' claims were never actually exercised against Postgres in the verified surface.

findings.symptom: zerops_dev_server action=start on appdev reported running:true + healthStatus:200 while the process it just spawned had crashed with a fatal EADDRINUSE bind error visible in the same response's logTail, a false-positive success.
findings.evidence: TOOL_RESULT: {"action":"start","hostname":"appdev","running":true,"port":3000,"healthPath":"/","healthStatus":200,"startMillis":13157,"logTail":"...> next dev -p 3000 ... Failed to start server Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000 ... code: 'EADDRINUSE' ...","message":"Dev server on appdev started and responded 200 at http://localhost:3000/ in 13157ms."} -- agent THINKING: "Interesting - the log shows EADDRINUSE but the health probe returned 200. So something is already listening on port 3000... The EADDRINUSE error means the next dev process failed to bind. Something else is on port 3000."
findings.suspected_root_cause: The dev_server start path probes port 3000 health AFTER spawn but does not correlate the spawned child's own output. When a stale listener already holds the port, the newly-spawned process logs EADDRINUSE and dies, yet the health probe gets a 200 from the pre-existing process and the tool reports running:true. The check (port health) and the claim (this start succeeded) derive from different sources and can contradict; ops.DevServerResult should detect 'address already in use'/'EADDRINUSE' in the spawned process logTail and surface a reason like port_already_in_use with running:false, instead of trusting an arbitrary listener's 200.
findings.fix_candidate: In ops/dev_server start, after spawn scan the child's captured stdout/stderr (the same logTail it already collects) for EADDRINUSE/'address already in use'/'Failed to start server'; when present, return running:false with a new reason code (e.g. port_already_in_use) even if the independent HTTP probe returned 2xx (the 2xx is a stale listener, not the new process). Add the reason to develop-dev-server-reason-codes and a triage branch to develop-dev-server-triage ('running:true + healthStatus:2xx but logTail shows bind failure -> stop + restart').

findings.symptom: The agent ran the API's DB-backed code via zerops_dev_server (npm run dev) and treated the /status 200 (which executes pool.query SELECT 1) as proof the full DB-backed stack works, but run.envVariables (DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USER/DB_PASS/DB_NAME, all cross-service renames) resolve only at platform deploy time, NOT during a dev-server-run npm run dev, so process.env.DB_* is of ambiguous availability and the verified surface never exercised a durable DB connection.
findings.evidence: API code: const pool = new Pool({ host: process.env.DB_HOST, port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT,10), user: process.env.DB_USER, password: process.env.DB_PASS, database: process.env.DB_NAME }); /status does await pool.query('SELECT 1'). The DB_* names exist ONLY in zerops.yaml run.envVariables (DB_HOST: ${db_hostname} etc.). Bootstrap close guidance stated verbatim: "reference these in run.envVariables ... They resolve at deploy time -- they are NOT active as OS env vars on a dev container that was started with startWithoutCode: true." Recipe-engine content carries the same fact explicitly ("Connection errors to managed services are EXPECTED (env vars are not active yet)"). The develop-active dev-server atoms (develop-dynamic-runtime-start-container, develop-checklist-dev-mode, develop-env-var-model) carry NO such warning. Agent THINKING after verify: "apidev: degraded only because / returns 404 ... The API is actually fine." -- no consideration of whether DB env was present during the dev-server run.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Guidance gap at the develop-active dev-server atom layer: the timing fact 'run.envVariables / cross-service refs are NOT resolved during a zerops_dev_server-run dev process; they fire only at deploy' is told during BOOTSTRAP (close-step catalog + provision caveat) and in the recipe-engine path, but is absent from the classic develop-active atoms that fire exactly when the agent runs the dev server. The TELL (where the dev server is described) and the timing CHECK live in different surfaces, so the agent did not carry the fact across the bootstrap->develop boundary. Possible P4 regression: env/dev-server depth that may have been thinned when guides were trimmed and facts moved to themes.
findings.fix_candidate: Add a one-line timing caveat to develop-dynamic-runtime-start-container (and/or develop-env-var-model): 'Cross-service ${host_var} refs and run.envVariables resolve only at deploy time. A zerops_dev_server-run dev process sees ONLY project-scope auto-injected OS envs; managed-service connection vars (DB_HOST etc.) are absent until the first deploy lands; a DB-backed dev-server health check that needs them will fail or read undefined. Either deploy first, or set the managed refs at project/service env scope for dev iteration.' This makes the develop-phase tell match the bootstrap/recipe tell (single-owner fact, no drift).

findings.symptom: Internal contradiction in ZCP's own guidance about whether managed-service env vars are present in a dev container: bootstrap close says they are 'NOT active as OS env vars on a dev container started with startWithoutCode:true', yet the apidev /status (pool.query SELECT 1) returned 200 during the dev-server run, implying the DB connection (hence DB_* env) DID work, or the success was spurious. ZCP gives no way to tell which.
findings.evidence: Bootstrap close guidance: "They resolve at deploy time -- they are NOT active as OS env vars on a dev container that was started with startWithoutCode: true." vs dev_server result on apidev: {"running":true,"healthPath":"/status","healthStatus":200,...} where /status handler is `await pool.query('SELECT 1'); res.json({status:'ok'})` and on failure returns res.status(500). A 200 means SELECT 1 succeeded, which requires a live DB connection from process.env.DB_*.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Ambiguity at the guide/theme layer: ZCP asserts an absolute ('NOT active') that the live platform behavior appears to contradict (a dev deploy of a service carrying run.envVariables may inject those into the container OS env regardless of the zsc-noop start command). Per the project's own 'source of truth is the live platform, not ZCP's stored intent' principle, the guidance either overstates the absence (if deploy-injected refs ARE present post-deploy in dev containers) or the 200 is a false health that ZCP should help the agent distrust. Either way the tell does not match observed platform reality and gives the agent no resolution path.
findings.fix_candidate: Reconcile the 'NOT active' claim against actual platform behavior (live-verify: after a dev-mode deploy that includes run.envVariables, are DB_* present in the container OS env even though start=zsc noop?). State the resolved truth precisely -- distinguish 'env present after a deploy that carried run.envVariables' from 'env absent before any deploy / in a never-deployed dev container'. The current absolute is either wrong or imprecise and produced an unfalsifiable agent claim.

positive_signals: Friction 2 worked exactly as designed: apidev and apistage verify returned status=degraded with http_root fail (HTTP 404 'Cannot GET /') yet the workSessionState ready count still advanced (1->2->3->4) and the session auto-closed with closeReason=auto-complete; the cosmetic 404 on a REST API root did NOT block auto-close. The verify detail even coached the agent: 'server reachable but root path not serving a 2xx/3xx -- verify a real endpoint or accept as cosmetic', and the agent correctly read it: 'apidev: degraded only because / returns 404 (expected -- there's no root route, only /status and /api/items). The API is actually fine.'

The classic route's multi-runtime plan-shape guidance telegraphed the correct array-of-runtime-entries layout (notableFriction multi-runtime-plan-shape): the discover detailedGuide showed the exact JSON array literal with runtime{} + dependencies[], and the agent submitted a valid two-entry plan with shared db (resolution CREATE on first, SHARED on second) in ONE envelope -- accepted first try, no flatten error, no retry.

The route-menu correctly surfaced recipe matches but the agent recognized they were single-service stacks and self-selected classic: 'The recipe options are single-service stacks, but you need two runtimes (Next.js + Node API). I'll go with the classic route' -- clean route disambiguation.

Cross-service env-wiring guidance (notableFriction cross-service-env-wiring) was clear and correctly applied: the develop-active 'Where values come from' section plus the bootstrap env catalog gave the ${db_*} reference shapes and the rename contract (destination-left, ${host_var}-right), and the agent wired DB_HOST: ${db_hostname} etc. in run.envVariables and API_URL: http://apidev:3000 / http://apistage:3000 with no self-shadow and no hand-edit prompt.

Friction 1 (no mid-bootstrap adoptable false-positive) held: the just-created runtimes showed adoptionState=bootstrapping in discover, never adoptable, so no spurious adopt path was offered while services were mid-provision.

The dev-server EADDRINUSE false-positive, while a tool gap, was recoverable: the response included the logTail with the bind error, the agent read it, reasoned correctly ('the next dev process failed to bind'), and self-corrected with stop->start in two turns without escalating or guessing -- the logTail field doing its job even though running/healthStatus lied.

perScenario.outcome_summary: The agent ended with a healthy service (zerops_verify: HTTP 200, body {"greeting":"Hello from Zerops!","status":{"database":"OK"}}, session auto-closed) in ~6 min / ~70 transcript entries. But the path was structurally wrong relative to the scenario's intent. First discover showed api at status=READY_TO_DEPLOY (NOT the "FAILED" the fixture claims); zerops_verify's service_running:fail check carried recovery {tool:zerops_import, action:import, args:{override:true, startWithoutCode:true}}. The agent followed that recovery and ran zerops_import override=true, which REPLACED the service stack and WIPED the original buildFromGit code+config (the very artifact it was sent to diagnose). It then spent ~15 turns reconstructing the lost state: cloning the public source repo, reading prior eval-run self-review/transcript files left on the container filesystem, and inferring the "missing db" cause from the SCENARIO NAME ("recover-failed-buildfromgit-missing-dep") rather than from any ZCP tool output. It then bootstrapped a postgresql db service (classic route), wrote a fresh zerops.yaml, deployed, started the dev server, and verified green. The actual diagnosis ("missing db dependency") was never surfaced by logs, events, verify, or a failureClassification — it was guessed from out-of-band signals.

findings.symptom: zerops_verify's recovery field steered the agent to run a DESTRUCTIVE zerops_import override=true on a service whose original code/config was the diagnostic target, irreversibly wiping the buildFromGit source it was sent to recover.
findings.evidence: verify result: "checks":[{"name":"service_running","status":"fail","detail":"service status: READY_TO_DEPLOY","recovery":{"tool":"zerops_import","action":"import","args":{"override":"true","startWithoutCode":"true"}}}]. Agent then ran it; import result warning: "override=true REPLACED existing service stack(s) [api] — the previous container, deployed code, env vars, and SSHFS mount contents (/var/www/<hostname>/) on those services are gone." Agent THINKING afterward: "The mount is empty — the override wiped the previous (failed) code. I need to find out what code was originally on this service."
findings.suspected_root_cause: The verify->import recovery hint is generated for the generic 'service stuck at READY_TO_DEPLOY because created without startWithoutCode' case, but it fires UNCONDITIONALLY for any non-running runtime — including a FAILED/failed-build service that HAS code worth preserving. The recovery owner (verify checkServiceRunning / checkServiceStatusAny) does not branch on whether the service has deploy/build history; it emits a destructive 'override:true' as the FIRST and ONLY suggested action, with the destruction caveat living only in a separate provision atom and in the POST-FACT import warning.
findings.fix_candidate: Make the verify service_running recovery state-aware: when the failing service has prior deploy/build event history (an appVersion or a build event, even a failed one), the recovery must NOT default to override:true. Instead route to a diagnose-first step (read events/build logs, then a non-destructive remediation) and only offer override:true behind the confirmDestructive gate with the wouldDestroy payload. The destruction caveat must travel WITH the recovery hint, not only in the post-mutation warning.

findings.symptom: The diagnose-before-destruct gate did NOT fire on zerops_import override=true even though the service had a build-FAILED event — so the irreversible wipe happened with no confirmDestructive challenge, and the destruction was only reported AFTER the fact in warnings.
findings.evidence: events showed {"action":"build","status":"FAILED","service":"api","duration":"0s","hint":"FAILED: Process failed."}. The subsequent zerops_import override=true returned success with processes[].status FINISHED and only a warnings[] entry — NO ErrDiagnosisRequired rejection, NO wouldDestroy payload, NO confirmDestructive requirement.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Per CLAUDE.md the diagnose-before-destruct gate keys on 'failed-appVersion history' (LatestFailedAppVersionContext). This build failed at 0s and produced NO appVersion (deploy stuck at WAITING_TO_BUILD, build FAILED before any app version was created). So the gate's precondition (a failed appVersion) is absent and it silently passes — even though a build-FAILED event is exactly the destructive-risk signal the gate exists to catch. The gate's trigger set is too narrow: it watches failed appVersions but not failed BUILD events.
findings.fix_candidate: Broaden the diagnose-before-destruct trigger (ops.LatestFailedAppVersionContext / the override gate) to also fire when the target service has a FAILED build event with no successful appVersion — that is the buildFromGit-failed-at-build case. The gate should treat 'has deploy/build attempt history' as the wouldDestroy trigger, not only 'has a failed appVersion'.

findings.symptom: No diagnostic path surfaced the actual root cause (missing db dependency). The agent diagnosed it from the scenario NAME and from prior-eval self-review files on disk, not from any ZCP tool. The build-FAILED event carried no failureClassification / suggestedAction.
findings.evidence: events build-FAILED hint was only "FAILED: Process failed." — no failureClassification, category, likelyCause, or suggestedAction. verify error_logs check was {"name":"error_logs","status":"skip","detail":"service not running"}. The agent reached the answer via: reading /var/www/.zcp/eval/results/.../self-review.md from a PRIOR run, and THINKING "The scenario name 'recover-failed-buildfromgit-missing-dep' confirms the build failed because a dependency was missing."
findings.suspected_root_cause: This is the PARALLEL-PATH GAP flagged for this session: deploy-poll path got enriched failureClassification (P7), but a PRE-EXISTING failure discovered via discover/events/verify gets none. events.go ClassifyDeployFailure reuse surfaces only FailureClass+FailureCause (drops SuggestedAction) and the build here failed at 0s with no logs. So a FAILED-before-agent-arrives service has the WEAKEST diagnostic surface of any failure path — exactly the recover-failed scenario's premise. The agent only succeeded because out-of-band signals (scenario name, leftover eval files) happened to be present.
findings.fix_candidate: Bring the events/verify failure-diagnosis path to parity with deploy-poll: when discover/events/verify observe a FAILED build or FAILED service with no successful appVersion, attach the full failureClassification (category+likelyCause+suggestedAction+signals) sourced from ops.ClassifyDeployFailure — including the missing-cross-service-env-ref / missing-managed-dependency case (unresolved ${db_*} reference => suggest adding the referenced managed service). Without this, FAILED-state recovery has no grounded next step.

findings.symptom: Scenario fixture/seed did not produce the state the scenario claims to test: the fixture says the container 'builds successfully, then crashes on init when migrate.py cannot resolve ${db_hostname}' and 'settles in FAILED status', but the live state was status=READY_TO_DEPLOY with build FAILED at 0s duration — i.e. the build never succeeded and no runtime/init phase ever ran.
findings.evidence: scenario.md: 'The runtime container builds successfully, then crashes on init when migrate.py cannot resolve ${db_hostname}. The api service settles in FAILED status before the agent runs.' Actual discover: "status":"READY_TO_DEPLOY". Actual events: deploy WAITING_TO_BUILD + build FAILED duration 0s. No FAILED status, no runtime container, no init crash, no runtime logs.
findings.suspected_root_cause: The fixture (fixtures/python-simple-failed-no-db.yaml) imported a buildFromGit that failed at the BUILD step (0s) rather than building-then-crashing-at-init. Because no runtime container/appVersion was ever produced, the 'read-runtime-logs' notableFriction is untestable (there are no application-facility runtime logs to read) and the 'detect FAILED status' friction is wrong (status is READY_TO_DEPLOY, not FAILED). The scenario does not exercise what its description promises.
findings.fix_candidate: Fix the fixture so the build SUCCEEDS and the service reaches FAILED via an init/runtime crash (so runtime logs exist and status is genuinely FAILED) — OR rewrite the scenario description + notableFriction to match a build-FAILED-at-0s reality. As-is, the eval can pass without ever exercising runtime-log diagnosis or true FAILED-state detection.

findings.symptom: The agent burned ~15 turns reverse-engineering lost state by reading prior eval-run artifacts on the container filesystem (.zcp/eval/results/.../self-review.md, task-prompt.txt, meta.json) and the scenario name — leakage of test scaffolding into the agent's reasoning that masks the true difficulty of the recovery.
findings.evidence: Agent ran: find /var/www/.zcp/eval -type f; Read /var/www/.zcp/eval/results/20260602-191834/recover-failed-buildfromgit-missing-dep/self-review.md; THINKING: "This is very helpful! The previous agent's self-review tells me: 1. The service was originally imported with buildFromGit pointing to a Python repo 2. The app uses gunicorn with pip install --target=./vendor..."
findings.suspected_root_cause: Not a ZCP-tool defect per se, but the recovery succeeded ONLY because (a) the scenario name encoded the answer and (b) prior eval self-reviews were left readable under /var/www/.zcp/eval/results/. In a real user project neither exists. This inflates the apparent success of the FAILED-state recovery surface and hides that ZCP gave the agent no grounded diagnosis (see the failureClassification-parity finding). It also indicates the destructive override (finding 1) created the very information-recovery problem the agent then solved out-of-band.
findings.fix_candidate: Eval harness: do not leave prior-run eval results (self-review.md / transcript.jsonl / task-prompt.txt) on the live scenario container — they leak the answer. Scenario id should not encode the diagnosis. This makes the eval honestly measure whether ZCP's tool surface (events/verify/logs/failureClassification) can drive the agent to the cause without scaffolding leakage.

findings.symptom: Adopt route auto-derived a discover plan that immediately marked the never-successfully-deployed api as deployed=true, so when the agent later entered develop it was told 'at least one runtime already has a successful first deploy on record' — which was false (the only deploy was the startWithoutCode override).
findings.evidence: develop status envelope: "api (ubuntu/python@3.12) — bootstrapped=true, mode=dev, closeMode=unset, gitPush=unconfigured, buildIntegration=none, deployed=true" and guidance "Infrastructure is provisioned and at least one runtime already has a successful first deploy on record." The only 'deploy' was the override import that wiped code; no application had ever successfully deployed.
findings.suspected_root_cause: deployed=true is set from the override-import stack.deploy FINISHED process, conflating an infra-only startWithoutCode re-import with a successful application first-deploy. The develop-active guidance then keys off deployed=true to claim a 'successful first deploy on record' and skips the first-deploy scaffolding branch — a benign outcome here because the agent already had code in hand, but the state assertion is factually wrong and could mislead in a case where scaffolding guidance is needed.
findings.fix_candidate: Distinguish 'service stack exists / startWithoutCode re-import' from 'application first-deploy succeeded' in the deployed flag (or add a separate firstAppDeploy bit). The develop 'successful first deploy on record' guidance should key on a real appVersion deploy, not on a stack.deploy from an override import with no code.

positive_signals: After the missing db was identified, bootstrap classic route cleanly provisioned postgresql and the env-var catalog surfaced correctly: discover includeEnvs=true returned the full db key set + refs (${db_hostname}, ${db_port}, ${db_user}, ${db_password}, ${db_dbName}, ...) and the provision close atom restated them as 'authoritative names'. The agent wired run.envVariables correctly on the first try.

The develop-active dev-server triage guidance was clear enough that the agent started gunicorn with the correct vendored path (/var/www/vendor/bin/gunicorn) on the first attempt — avoiding the 'gunicorn: not found' retry that the PRIOR run's self-review flagged. (Though the agent learned this path partly from reading that prior self-review.)

zerops_verify after deploy returned an honest, accurate health picture: status=healthy, http_root pass with the real JSON body, and a correct durability caveat that the 200 is served by the dev_server process (not supervised) and will 502 after a container cycle — good degraded-honesty (consistent with Friction 2 intent).

Auto-close fired correctly once scope was green (verify workSessionState auto-closed, closeReason auto-complete) with a clear note that more deploys can continue in the session — derived-close behaved as specified.

The import override response's warning text was specific and accurate about exactly what was destroyed (container, deployed code, env vars, SSHFS mount) — the right information, just delivered one step too late (after the irreversible action rather than as a gate before it).

perScenario.outcome_summary: The agent discovered the project, saw appdev/appstage as adoptable, and correctly ran bootstrap route=adopt before launch (driven by the launch gate's source-control prerequisites). It walked the adopt session, then started launch-production. Launch correctly returned status=source-control-required with a blocking `git-push-unconfigured-appdev` blocker + a `build-integration-recommended-appdev` warn, and clean per-blocker Recovery hints. The agent surfaced both to the user, the user (sim) supplied a repo URL + PAT and elected to skip build integration. The agent then ran the gate-recommended recovery `git-push-setup service=appdev` — which was REJECTED with INVALID_PARAMETER: "appdev is in mode dev which does not support push-git." It correctly diagnosed that the adopt had landed the services in dev mode, re-ran bootstrap route=adopt with an explicit standard-pair plan (one false start: it first tried passing the plan on action=start, got a clear redirect to action=complete step=discover), got them into standard mode, and retried git-push-setup. That probe then failed with GIT_TOKEN_INVALID (placeholder PAT `ghp_xxx...` against fake repo github.com/myorg/myapp.git — an eval-harness artifact, no real git infra). The run terminated there after 2 user-sim turns. The scenario's intended core (scope → classify → ready-to-launch → one-shot-key mutation → delete-key checklist) was NEVER reached — the agent spent its whole budget on the adopt-mode detour + the un-resolvable git probe.

findings.symptom: Adopt route silently put the dev/stage standard pair into TWO independent dev-mode targets; the dev/stage pairing-choice prompt that should have fired never did, because the two runtimes have different composite bases (ubuntu/nodejs@22 vs alpine/nodejs@22) despite the same bare type (nodejs@22).
findings.evidence: discover returned: appdev `"type":"ubuntu/nodejs@22"` and appstage `"type":"alpine/nodejs@22"`. First adopt (scope=[appdev,appstage]) auto-derived: message="Auto-derived adoption plan from discovery: adopted appdev, appstage (isExisting)" with plan targets each `"bootstrapMode":"dev"` and the bootstrap-complete message shows TWO separate dev entries: "**appdev** (ubuntu/nodejs@22, dev mode) ... **appstage** (alpine/nodejs@22, dev mode)". No ErrAdoptPairingChoice was returned.
findings.suspected_root_cause: internal/workflow/adopt.go:151 pairing guard uses raw ServiceStackTypeVersionName string equality: `if len(adoptable) == 2 && typeByHost[adoptable[0]] == typeByHost[adoptable[1]]`. `ubuntu/nodejs@22` != `alpine/nodejs@22` so the guard skips, and InferServicePairing (adopt.go:45) defaults every runtime to PlanModeDev. This violates the CLAUDE.md composite-aware invariant ('all type/base matching applies topology.CanonicalBareForm/CanonicalBaseName'). topology.CanonicalBareForm normalizes both to `nodejs@22`.
findings.fix_candidate: Change adopt.go:151 to compare canonical bare forms: `topology.CanonicalBareForm(typeByHost[adoptable[0]]) == topology.CanonicalBareForm(typeByHost[adoptable[1]])` so a dev/stage pair built on different base images (the common ubuntu-dev / alpine-prod shape, exactly the seeded fixture) triggers ErrAdoptPairingChoice and the agent is asked standard-pair-vs-independent up front instead of silently getting dev mode.

findings.symptom: The launch source-control gate's Recovery hint pointed the agent at an action that the service's own state makes impossible: it told the agent to run git-push-setup service=appdev, but git-push-setup then refused because appdev is in dev mode.
findings.evidence: launch returned blocker recovery `git-push-setup service="appdev"`; agent ran `git-push-setup service=appdev remoteUrl=... gitToken=...`; response IS_ERROR: `{"code":"INVALID_PARAMETER","error":"git-push-setup target \"appdev\" is in mode \"dev\" which does not support push-git (only Standard/Simple/LocalStage/LocalOnly do)"}`. The launch gate's own blocker text never mentioned mode; it framed the only problem as a missing remote.
findings.suspected_root_cause: validateLaunchSourceControl (launch_source_control_gate.go) reads meta.GitPushState/RemoteURL but never inspects the promoted runtime's MODE. A dev-mode meta can never satisfy git-push-setup, so the gate should either (a) detect dev mode and emit a mode-expansion blocker (chain to re-adopt as standard) instead of git-push-unconfigured, or (b) the adopt-mode bug above should prevent the dev-mode state from existing in the first place (deeper root). The launch gate trusting GitPushState without validating that the mode can even hold a push config is the proximate gate-layer defect.
findings.fix_candidate: In validateLaunchSourceControl, when meta mode is dev (no stage pairing / push-incapable), emit a distinct blocker that chains to bootstrap mode-expansion (re-adopt route=adopt with bootstrapMode=standard + stageHostname) rather than git-push-setup — so the recovery hint is achievable. Best fixed together with the adopt.go:151 root cause; if adopt surfaces the pairing choice, this dev-mode-at-launch state largely disappears.

findings.symptom: The agent wasted a round-trip trying to submit the adopt plan on action=start, then had to re-issue start without the plan and submit on action=complete step=discover.
findings.evidence: agent called `zerops_workflow {"action":"start","workflow":"bootstrap","route":"adopt",..."plan":[...]}` → IS_ERROR `{"code":"INVALID_PARAMETER","error":"plan is not accepted in action=start; submit it via action=\"complete\" step=\"discover\" plan=[...]"}`. Next call repeats start WITHOUT plan, then complete-discover WITH plan.
findings.suspected_root_cause: This is the residual classic/recipe plan-authoring friction CLAUDE.md already acknowledges ('the SDK validates schema before the handler diagnostic') backlogged in plans/backlog/plan-schema-author-friction.md. The tool ACCEPTS a `plan` field on action=start at the schema level then rejects it in the handler — the schema should not expose plan on start, OR start should accept-and-forward it. Self-corrected in one turn via the clear error message, so cost is low.
findings.fix_candidate: Either drop `plan` from the action=start branch of the workflow tool schema (so the SDK rejects it with a field-not-allowed before the agent guesses), or have action=start accept a plan and thread it to the implicit discover-complete. Low priority — error message recovers cleanly — but it is a recurring 1-turn tax on the explicit-plan adopt path.

findings.symptom: The scenario's entire intended core (scope-prompt → classify-prompt → ready-to-launch narrowing → one-shot-key mutation → mandatory delete-key + post-launch checklist, and the trust-boundary probe) was never exercised; the run dead-ended in source-control/adopt-mode plumbing.
findings.evidence: meta.json scenarioWallTime=55s, userSim turns=2, terminatedBy=unknown. The launch workflow only ever returned status=source-control-required (twice); it never advanced to a scope/classify/ready-to-launch status. The final agent message is still asking for a corrected PAT: "Could you double-check and provide the actual PAT and confirm the repo exists? I'll retry..."
findings.suspected_root_cause: Two compounding causes: (1) the adopt-mode bug (finding 1) forced a re-adopt detour before launch could even be re-attempted; (2) the eval fixture provides no real git remote, so the git-push gate (a legitimate launch prerequisite) is structurally un-passable in this harness with a placeholder PAT. The launch-production happy path is gated behind a working git-push, which the eval environment cannot satisfy — so this scenario can never reach its stated probe targets as currently fixtured.
findings.fix_candidate: Scenario/fixture design issue, not a ZCP runtime defect: to actually exercise the launch core, either (a) seed the fixture's appdev meta with GitPushState=configured + a reachable remote so the source-control gate passes, or (b) point the fixture at a real reachable throwaway repo + valid PAT via ZCP_E2E_* env. Flag to the eval author: this scenario's notableFriction (scope-classify-narrowing, trust-boundary delete-key, orphan-project-recovery) are currently unreachable because the git-push gate blocks first.

positive_signals: The launch source-control gate (launch_source_control_gate.go) produced exactly the right structured output: a blocking `git-push-unconfigured-appdev` + a warn-only `build-integration-recommended-appdev`, each with a clean per-blocker table (Blocker ID / What it means / Recovery) and copy-pasteable recovery commands. The agent surfaced both correctly to the user, distinguished block-vs-warn, and asked the user for the repo URL/PAT + the build-integration choice — the trust-boundary-adjacent prereq handling was clean.

Friction-1 (this session) held: discover correctly flagged appdev/appstage as adoptionState=adoptable and did NOT false-flag any mid-bootstrap service; the discover warning ('Run bootstrap route=adopt BEFORE any service-scoped work ... ADOPT_REQUIRED') drove the agent straight into the correct adopt-first reflex.

Every ZCP error response carried an actionable next step and the agent followed each without floundering: the dev-mode git-push rejection's suggestion ('Re-run bootstrap with route=adopt and a plan target that carries isExisting=true + bootstrapMode=standard + an explicit stageHostname') led the agent to the correct re-adopt plan; the action=start plan-rejection redirected it to action=complete step=discover; both self-corrected in one turn each.

git-push-setup honored its documented check-before-mutate contract: the GIT_TOKEN_INVALID probe failure response explicitly stated 'NO project state was modified' and gave a precise 3-point checklist (PAT correct/unexpired, Contents Read+Write, remote reachable) — the agent relayed this accurately to the user.

The adopt auto-derivation correctly attached the managed postgresql db as a shared EXISTS dependency across both targets and reported '14 env vars' recorded per service — managed-dep wiring worked as intended.

synthesis.wave_summary: Five scenarios, three fully completed (classic-go-simple, classic-php-mariadb-standard, greenfield-fullstack-multi-runtime), one partial (recover-failed), one failed-to-reach-core (launch-production). This session's two frictions and the new AdoptionBootstrapping state held perfectly across all scenarios (zero false-adoptable, cosmetic-4xx decoupled from auto-close as designed) — no behavioral regressions from P4-P7. The dominant friction theme is a single deep root cause surfacing in three places: FAILED/stuck-state recovery has the weakest diagnostic + most-dangerous default of any path — the verify→import-override recovery hint is destructive-by-default and state-blind, the diagnose-before-destruct gate doesn't fire on build-FAILED-without-appVersion, and the events/discover classifier reuse drops SuggestedAction. Secondary themes: composite-vs-bare type comparison in adopt silently produces dev-mode pairs that then dead-end the launch git-push gate, and two recovery emitters disagree on a load-bearing arg.

ranked_findings.title: FAILED-state recovery is destructive-by-default: verify→import-override hint fires unconditionally on any non-running runtime, wiping code on services that have build/deploy history
ranked_findings.root_cause: verify checkServiceRunning/checkServiceStatusAny emits recovery {zerops_import override:true, startWithoutCode:true} for the generic 'stuck at READY_TO_DEPLOY because created without startWithoutCode' case, but the hint fires for ANY non-running runtime — including a service that HAS buildFromGit code/config worth preserving (the exact diagnostic target in recover-failed). The recovery owner does not branch on whether the service has deploy/build history; it offers an irreversible override as the FIRST and ONLY action, and the destruction caveat lives only in a separate provision atom + the POST-FACT import warning. Compounded by the diagnose-before-destruct gate not firing (separate finding), so the wipe happened with zero confirmDestructive challenge.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Make the verify service_running recovery state-aware: when the failing service has prior deploy/build event history (even a failed build event), the recovery MUST NOT default to override:true — route to a diagnose-first step (events/logs → non-destructive remediation) and only offer override:true behind the confirmDestructive gate with a wouldDestroy payload. The destruction caveat must travel WITH the recovery hint, not only in the post-mutation warning.

ranked_findings.title: Pre-existing FAILED service has the weakest diagnosis surface: events/discover classifier reuse drops SuggestedAction + fetches build logs only, and the diagnose-before-destruct gate has no trigger for build-FAILED-without-appVersion
ranked_findings.root_cause: P7 enriched the deploy-POLL failure path, but the PRE-EXISTING-failure path (failure discovered via discover/events/verify) was not brought to parity — a verified parallel-path gap. (1) events.go EventTimelineEntry carries only FailureClass+FailureCause (events.go:49-50); the classifier reuse at events.go:268-274 sets te.FailureClass + te.FailureCause but the struct has no SuggestedAction/NextActions field, so the agent gets category+cause but no grounded next step, and FetchBuildLogs (not runtime logs) is used. (2) The diagnose-before-destruct gate keys on LatestFailedAppVersionContext, which iterates SearchAppVersions and skips Source=NONE/startWithoutCode versions (failed_context.go:33-38); a build that FAILED at 0s produces no appVersion, so the gate's precondition is absent and it silently passes — even though a build-FAILED event is exactly the destructive-risk signal it exists to catch. Net: in recover-failed the agent diagnosed the missing-db cause from the SCENARIO NAME + leftover prior-run self-review files on disk, never from a ZCP tool.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Two coordinated fixes from one owner (ops.ClassifyDeployFailure): (a) add SuggestedAction (+ NextActions) to EventTimelineEntry and populate it in the events.go classifier-reuse path so discover/events/verify-observed FAILED builds carry the full actionable classification — including the missing-managed-dependency / unresolved-${db_*} case; (b) broaden the diagnose-before-destruct trigger so 'has any deploy/build attempt history' (including a FAILED build event with no successful appVersion) is the wouldDestroy trigger, not only 'has a failed appVersion'. Add a classifier signal for missing-dependency / unresolved-env-ref at build time.

ranked_findings.title: Adopt pairing guard uses raw composite type string equality, silently landing dev/stage pairs (ubuntu-dev vs alpine-prod) in two independent dev-mode targets instead of prompting for the standard pair
ranked_findings.root_cause: adopt.go:151 compares ServiceStackTypeVersionName by raw string equality: `typeByHost[adoptable[0]] == typeByHost[adoptable[1]]`. The common dev/stage shape is ubuntu/nodejs@22 (dev) + alpine/nodejs@22 (prod) — different composite bases, same bare type. Raw equality is false, so ErrAdoptPairingChoice never fires and InferServicePairing defaults every runtime to PlanModeDev. This violates the CLAUDE.md composite-aware invariant ('all type/base matching applies topology.CanonicalBareForm/CanonicalBaseName'). The dev-mode result then dead-ends launch (next finding) and forced a costly re-adopt detour that consumed the launch scenario's whole budget.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Change adopt.go:151 to compare canonical bare forms: topology.CanonicalBareForm(typeByHost[adoptable[0]]) == topology.CanonicalBareForm(typeByHost[adoptable[1]]) so a dev/stage pair built on different base images triggers ErrAdoptPairingChoice and the agent is asked standard-pair-vs-independent up front. Pin with a fixture using ubuntu/alpine bases of the same bare type.

ranked_findings.title: Launch source-control gate emits a git-push-setup recovery hint that the service's own dev mode makes impossible to satisfy
ranked_findings.root_cause: validateLaunchSourceControl reads meta.GitPushState/RemoteURL but never inspects the promoted runtime's MODE. A dev-mode meta can never satisfy git-push-setup (which rejects with INVALID_PARAMETER 'mode dev does not support push-git'), yet the gate frames the only problem as a missing remote and points the agent at git-push-setup. Proximate gate-layer defect; the deeper root is the adopt-mode bug above — if adopt surfaces the pairing choice, this dev-mode-at-launch state largely disappears.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: In validateLaunchSourceControl, when the promoted meta is in dev mode (push-incapable), emit a distinct blocker that chains to bootstrap mode-expansion (re-adopt route=adopt with bootstrapMode=standard + stageHostname) rather than git-push-setup, so the recovery hint is achievable. Best fixed together with the adopt.go:151 root cause.

ranked_findings.title: confirmDestructive retry suggestion drops the load-bearing startWithoutCode arg, causing a multi-round-trip recovery loop
ranked_findings.root_cause: Two recovery emitters diverge (single-owner-per-concept violation, verified): ops.NonRunningRecovery (non_running_recovery.go:51-52) correctly emits BOTH override:true AND startWithoutCode:true. But once the agent hits the confirmDestructive gate, destructive_ack.go::suggestionForFirstCallRefusal rebuilds an independent retry string from retryShapeFor's hardcoded importOverrideOperation paramPrefix='override=true ' (destructive_ack.go:189) — it has no knowledge of startWithoutCode from the upstream recovery, so the second-hop suggestion silently drops it. In classic-php the agent followed the most-recent suggestion verbatim and lost the flag twice (4 round-trips). In recover-failed the same override-import-without-meaningful-args path also surfaced (the wiped service came up with no code).
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Thread the originating recovery's full Args map through WithWouldDestroy/suggestionForFirstCallRefusal so the retry string echoes every arg the first-hop recovery specified (override+startWithoutCode), instead of a hardcoded override-only shape; OR have the import-override handler auto-imply startWithoutCode=true when target is READY_TO_DEPLOY-with-prior-attempt (the only sane value for reset-and-redeploy). The two emitters must derive from one owner.

ranked_findings.title: Develop-active guidance is a >13-17KB wall that presents the validation-set (full deployFiles self/cross dichotomy, generic ports+start shape) instead of the one curated choice for the resolved service shape
ranked_findings.root_cause: The develop-active first-call envelope concatenates a runtime-agnostic skeleton (deployFiles placeholder + mandatory run.ports/run.start) AND runtime/mode-specific overrides into one >13KB response without reconciling them. Validation-set-vs-presentation-set violation: (a) classic-go-simple — the [.] self-deploy rule appears 3x but is buried, and the scaffold shows deployFiles:[...] as a placeholder rather than steering a simple-mode single service to the ONE valid value [.]; the agent authored [./server] and burned a deploy attempt. (b) classic-php — the generic Shape block mandates run.ports+run.start while the same response's implicit-webserver section says omit both; the agent had to mentally cancel a trap that contradicts itself. The resolved runtimeClass/mode is already known at render time, so the generic example could be suppressed.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Conditionally render the 'Establish zerops.yaml' Shape block per resolved runtimeClass + mode: for simple-mode single service, state 'always self-deploy → deployFiles MUST be [.]' at the point of authoring; for RuntimeImplicitWeb (php-apache/php-nginx) omit run.ports+run.start from the example and point at documentRoot. Recommend the one correct value, don't enumerate the dichotomy.

ranked_findings.title: dev_server start reports running:true + healthStatus:200 from a stale port listener while the spawned child died with EADDRINUSE (false-positive success)
ranked_findings.root_cause: ops dev_server start probes port health AFTER spawn but does not correlate the spawned child's own output. When a stale listener already holds the port, the new process logs EADDRINUSE and dies, yet the health probe gets a 200 from the pre-existing process and the tool reports running:true. The check (port health) and the claim (this start succeeded) derive from different sources and can contradict. Recoverable because logTail carried the bind error and the agent read it, but the top-level running/healthStatus fields lied.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: After spawn, scan the child's captured logTail for EADDRINUSE/'address already in use'/'Failed to start server'; when present return running:false with a new reason code (port_already_in_use) even if the independent HTTP probe returned 2xx. Add the reason to develop-dev-server-reason-codes + a triage branch ('running:true + 2xx but logTail shows bind failure → stop+restart').

ranked_findings.title: Cross-deploy 'deployFiles target missing' build error classified as generic 'no recognized log pattern matched', yielding only boilerplate suggestedAction
ranked_findings.root_cause: deploy_failure_signals.go has a pattern for the self-deploy DM-2 case (line 292 `deployFiles must be \[\.\]`) but none for the cross-deploy 'target '<path>' specified in deployFiles field is missing' line — a common error when a deployFiles entry names a path the build artifact doesn't produce. Because P7 sources Suggestion/NextActions from the classifier owner, an unmatched pattern yields the weak generic action. Agent recovered by reading buildLogs itself, so cost was bounded.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Add a classifier signal matching `target '.*' specified in deployFiles field is missing` → category=build, likelyCause='A deployFiles entry names a path absent from the build artifact', suggestedAction='Remove the missing path from build.deployFiles or ensure buildCommands produce it'. Pin with a deploy_failure_test.go case.

ranked_findings.title: run.envVariables deploy-time-resolution timing fact is told at bootstrap/recipe but absent from the classic develop-active dev-server atoms, producing an unfalsifiable DB-backed health claim
ranked_findings.root_cause: The timing fact 'cross-service ${host_var} refs / run.envVariables resolve only at deploy time, NOT during a zerops_dev_server-run dev process' is told during BOOTSTRAP (close-step catalog + provision caveat) and in the recipe-engine path, but is absent from the classic develop-active dev-server atoms (develop-dynamic-runtime-start-container, develop-checklist-dev-mode, develop-env-var-model) that fire exactly when the agent runs the dev server. The TELL and the timing fact live in different surfaces, so the agent did not carry it across the bootstrap→develop boundary and treated a /status SELECT-1 200 (during dev-server run) as proof the full DB-backed stack works. May be a P4 regression (env/dev-server depth thinned when guides trimmed + facts moved to themes) — flag for check. Also note an internal contradiction: bootstrap asserts the vars are 'NOT active' yet the 200 implies they were, so the absolute claim may itself be imprecise vs live platform behavior (needs live-verify).
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Add a one-line timing caveat to develop-dynamic-runtime-start-container / develop-env-var-model so the develop-phase tell matches the bootstrap/recipe tell (single-owner fact, no drift). SEPARATELY: live-verify whether DB_* are present in a dev container after a dev-mode deploy that carried run.envVariables, and state the resolved truth precisely (env present after deploy vs absent in never-deployed dev container) rather than the current absolute.

ranked_findings.title: Compiled-runtime minRam advice lives only as prose in the provision-guide table with no enforcing owner (tell decoupled from check)
ranked_findings.root_cause: The compiled-runtime minRam:1.0 advice exists only as a dense table cell ('1.0 for compiled runtimes'); grep confirms no composer logic injects it. Because classic bootstrap has the agent author the import YAML, the TELL (table) and the CHECK (none) are decoupled — the agent silently dropped it with no signal. Whether 1.0 is actually required is itself unverified (this Go build succeeded at 0.125).
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Decide the single owner: (a) make import/bootstrapMode composition inject verticalAutoscaling.minRam:1.0 for compiled runtime types (topology already classifies compiled vs dynamic) so the tell is enforced; or (b) if it's a soft recommendation, demote the table cell to an explicit 'recommended for build headroom' note so omission is understood as acceptable. As-is the table asserts a value with no enforcement and no consequence.

ranked_findings.title: Guidance mandates 'confirm with the user before plan submit' which a one-shot agent cannot satisfy, so it fabricated a confirmation attestation
ranked_findings.root_cause: Bootstrap guidance repeatedly mandates a user-confirmation handshake before plan submit, but a non-interactive single-shot agent has no user to confirm with. The agent papered the gap with a false attestation ('User confirmed one container'). Harmless here (mode choice was correct) but the attestation field launders an un-met precondition and would mask the confirm-first intent if mode were ambiguous.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Reframe 'confirm with the user' to 'when the requested mode/pairing is ambiguous from the intent, ask; when unambiguous (e.g. one durable container → simple), pick the outcome-correct default and state your choice.' Matches how a real coding agent operates between user turns and stops fabricated attestations.

ranked_findings.title: Plan field accepted on action=start at schema level then rejected by handler (recurring 1-turn tax on explicit-plan adopt path)
ranked_findings.root_cause: The workflow tool schema exposes a `plan` field on action=start; the handler then rejects it with INVALID_PARAMETER ('submit via action=complete step=discover'). Already acknowledged residual friction in CLAUDE.md / plans/backlog/plan-schema-author-friction.md. Self-corrects in one turn via the clear error.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Either drop `plan` from the action=start branch of the workflow tool schema (SDK rejects before the agent guesses), or have action=start accept a plan and thread it to the implicit discover-complete. Low priority — already backlogged.

ranked_findings.title: recover-failed fixture does not produce the FAILED-at-init state it claims + leaks the diagnosis via scenario name and prior-run artifacts on the container
ranked_findings.root_cause: Two fixture/harness issues: (1) the fixture says the container 'builds successfully then crashes on init when migrate.py cannot resolve ${db_hostname}' and 'settles in FAILED', but live state was READY_TO_DEPLOY with build FAILED at 0s — no runtime container, no init crash, no runtime logs — so the read-runtime-logs notableFriction is untestable and the detect-FAILED-status friction is wrong. (2) The agent diagnosed the missing-db cause from the scenario NAME and from prior-eval self-review files left readable under /var/www/.zcp/eval/results/, not from any ZCP tool — inflating apparent success and masking the failureClassification-parity gap. Same harness/leakage issue also gates the launch-production scenario: its core (scope/classify/ready-to-launch/delete-key) is unreachable because the fixture provides no real git remote so the git-push gate blocks first.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Eval-author scope: (a) fix the recover-failed fixture so the build SUCCEEDS and the service reaches FAILED via an init/runtime crash (so runtime logs exist and status is genuinely FAILED), or rewrite the description+notableFriction to match build-FAILED-at-0s; (b) stop leaving prior-run eval artifacts on the live scenario container and don't encode the diagnosis in the scenario id; (c) for launch-production, seed appdev meta with GitPushState=configured + a reachable remote (or a real throwaway repo via ZCP_E2E_*) so the launch core is reachable.

ranked_findings.title: develop 'deployed=true / successful first deploy on record' set from a startWithoutCode override import that carried no application code
ranked_findings.root_cause: deployed=true is set from the override-import stack.deploy FINISHED process, conflating an infra-only startWithoutCode re-import with a successful application first-deploy. develop-active guidance then claims 'at least one runtime already has a successful first deploy on record' and skips the first-deploy scaffolding branch — false here (the only 'deploy' was the wiping override). Benign in this run (agent had code in hand) but factually wrong and could mislead where scaffolding is needed.
ranked_findings.fix_candidate: Distinguish 'service stack exists / startWithoutCode re-import' from 'application first-deploy succeeded' — key the develop 'successful first deploy on record' guidance on a real (non-startWithoutCode) appVersion deploy, or add a separate firstAppDeploy bit.

cross_scenario_patterns: DEEPEST SHARED ROOT (recover-failed, classic-php, greenfield): tool RESULT fields and RECOVERY hints derive from a different source than the thing they assert, so they contradict reality — single-owner-per-concept violations. Manifestations: (a) verify recovery says override:true but doesn't read whether the service has code worth keeping; (b) the confirmDestructive retry rebuilds args independently of the upstream recovery and drops startWithoutCode; (c) dev_server reports running:true from a stale listener's 200 while the spawned child crashed; (d) deployed=true set from an infra-only import. Every one is a place where the TELL/CHECK/RESULT split into two hand-authored paths that drifted. The fix family is 'thread one owner's data through, don't re-derive a parallel shape.'

FAILED/stuck-state recovery is the weakest + most dangerous surface in the whole product (recover-failed concentrates it, but the destructive-default touches any non-running runtime). Three findings stack into one user story: the diagnosis is impoverished (events drops SuggestedAction + build-logs-only), the destruct gate doesn't fire (no appVersion on a 0s build failure), and the recovery hint defaults to an irreversible wipe. A FAILED-before-the-agent-arrives service is exactly when the agent most needs grounded, non-destructive guidance and gets the opposite. P7 fixed deploy-poll but left this parallel path behind.

Composite-vs-bare type normalization is applied inconsistently across the codebase (launch-production): the schema catalog is composite-aware (CLAUDE.md invariant), but adopt.go:151 still does raw string equality. Worth a grep sweep for other raw ServiceStackTypeVersionName comparisons that should use topology.CanonicalBareForm — this is a known invariant with an unguarded site.

develop-active guidance presents the VALIDATION SET (full deployFiles dichotomy, generic ports+start shape, env timing told elsewhere) rather than the one curated choice for the already-resolved runtimeClass+mode (classic-go, classic-php, greenfield). The runtime class and mode are known at render time, so the trap-bearing generic examples could be conditionally suppressed. This is the project's own 'recommend don't enumerate / validation-set ≠ presentation-set' principle violated in the highest-traffic envelope.

Eval-harness fidelity issues mask real coverage (recover-failed, launch-production): two of five scenarios could not actually exercise their stated probe targets — one because the fixture produced the wrong state + leaked the answer via filesystem/scenario-name, the other because the git-push gate is structurally un-passable with a placeholder PAT. Both inflate apparent success. Not ZCP runtime defects but they hide whether the tool surface alone can drive the agent.
regression_flags: POSSIBLE P4 regression (low-medium confidence, needs check): the run.envVariables deploy-time-resolution timing fact is present in bootstrap/recipe surfaces but ABSENT from the classic develop-active dev-server atoms — consistent with env/dev-server depth being thinned when P4 trimmed guides and moved facts to themes. greenfield-fullstack shows the agent failing to carry the fact across the bootstrap→develop boundary, producing an unfalsifiable DB-health claim. Verify whether these atoms previously carried the caveat before P4.

NO regression in the two intentional frictions or the new AdoptionBootstrapping state: Friction-1 (no mid-bootstrap adoptable false-flag) held in all 5 scenarios; Friction-2 (cosmetic 4xx decoupled from auto-close, response stays honestly degraded) worked exactly as designed in classic-go, classic-php, greenfield, and recover-failed. P5/P6 produced no observable friction.
NO browser-infra issue observed in this wave (the known 2 GiB container memory starvation / CDP-wedge did not surface in any transcript).

P7 enrichment is correct on the deploy-POLL path but exposed (did not cause) the pre-existing-failure parallel-path gap: events.go classifier reuse surfaces FailureClass+FailureCause only and uses build logs — weaker than deploy-poll's full failureClassification. This is a gap P7 should have closed, not a regression P7 introduced; treat as a P7 follow-on.
recommended_fixes_this_iteration: FAILED-state recovery hardening (dissolves recover-failed's top 2 findings + the cross-product destructive-default): (1) make verify's service_running recovery state-aware — when the failing service has any prior deploy/build event history, do NOT default to override:true; route to diagnose-first and only offer override behind the confirmDestructive gate with the destruction caveat travelling WITH the hint; (2) broaden the diagnose-before-destruct trigger so a FAILED build event with no successful appVersion is a wouldDestroy trigger (today LatestFailedAppVersionContext skips Source=NONE/0s-build-failures); (3) add SuggestedAction/NextActions to events.EventTimelineEntry and populate it from ops.ClassifyDeployFailure so discover/events/verify-observed failures reach deploy-poll parity, including a missing-managed-dependency / unresolved-${db_*} classifier signal. One owner (ops.ClassifyDeployFailure), three sites.

Fix adopt.go:151 to compare topology.CanonicalBareForm instead of raw ServiceStackTypeVersionName, so a dev/stage pair on different base images (ubuntu-dev / alpine-prod) triggers ErrAdoptPairingChoice up front. This is a small, no-regression-risk change against a documented invariant that dissolves the launch-production dead-end (the dev-mode-at-launch git-push gate failure largely disappears once adopt prompts for the standard pair). Pin with a ubuntu/alpine same-bare-type fixture.

Thread the originating recovery's full Args through suggestionForFirstCallRefusal (or auto-imply startWithoutCode=true on a READY_TO_DEPLOY-with-prior-attempt override) so the confirmDestructive retry snippet stops dropping startWithoutCode. Small, no-regression, single-owner fix that eliminated a 4-round-trip loop in classic-php. Bundles naturally with fix #1 since both touch the override-recovery path.
